newsitem.title: ITALY: World Food Summit adopts plan to fight hunger.
newsitem.headline: World Food Summit adopts plan to fight hunger.

text.p: A World Food Summit adopted a plan on Wednesday to halve the number of people who suffer chronic hunger and malnutrition by the year 2015 from the present 840 million.

The commitment was contained in a Declaration on World Food Security and a Plan of Action on how to achieve food for all that was approved by acclamation at the first working session of the 194-nation, five-day summit.

The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation, which is holding the summit, says the world will need to produce 75 percent more food in the next 30 years to feed three billion more people as the population jumps from 5.7 billion to 8.7 billion by 2030.

The agency's director-general Jacques Diouf, who is from Senegal, urged world leaders in a speech at the opening ceremony of the summit to make sure they lived up to the commitments they made in the documents, which are not legally binding.

"These so commendable international decisions risk turning sour if, when taking stock in a few years time, we see that hopes have been dashed, unless measures are taken here and now to mould these decisions into national projects and programmes," Diouf said.
A senior summit official said an unspecified number of countries had submitted written "reservations and interpretative statements" on the documents. He did not elaborate.
